research_domain_title: Citizen-Service Government, Public Office Equality, and Civic Access
note: Major Public Service Doctrine plus Citizen-Service Government institutional design. Eliminates office-tied privilege while making service accessible to ordinary working people. Separates temporary democratic leadership from professional public administration. Architecture only — no invented program costs, employer-subsidy amounts, or current benefit-package statistics. Leave, funds, cooling-off, and commission design require legal drafting (legal remains 0%).
central_theme: Public office is an act of constitutional service, not a pathway to a privileged class.

operational_principle.text: Serve without sacrifice. Govern without privilege. Return without penalty.

governing_principle.text: No elected office shall create a permanent political class. Those entrusted with public office remain citizens first and shall participate in the same fundamental retirement, healthcare, and social systems available to the people they serve.

accessibility_doctrine.text: No citizen should have to sacrifice their livelihood, business, career, family security, or retirement in order to serve their community in public office.
accessibility_doctrine.supporting: Public service should be a respected chapter in a productive life—not a separate political profession.
accessibility_doctrine.guiding_doctrine: Public government should draw leadership from the full productive life of the community. No capable citizen should be excluded from public service because they cannot afford to abandon a job, business, family, or profession. The republic must protect the citizen’s pathway into service, support competent performance while serving, and guarantee a dignified return to community life afterward.

constitutional_principle.text: Public office confers responsibility, not privilege. Elected officials shall remain participants in the same civic systems they establish for the people. No office shall create a permanent political class or guarantee lifelong benefits unavailable to similarly situated citizens. The highest reward for faithful public service is the continued trust and respect of a free people, not permanent governmental privilege.
constitutional_principle.alignment_theme: Those who govern should experience the consequences—good or bad—of the systems they create.

leadership_vs_administration.objective_not: Eliminate experienced public servants. Government needs institutional knowledge and professional administration.

separate.temporary_democratic_leadership: Exercised by citizens; sets direction; accountable to voters.
separate.professional_public_administration: Performed by trained career personnel; administers programs competently and impartially.

earned_vs_privilege_distinction.framing: Eliminate special privileges tied to office rather than take away benefits someone has earned through prior service or contributions under the same rules as everyone else.
earned_vs_privilege_distinction.same_rules: If an elected official contributes to the same retirement system as everyone else under the same rules, they receive the same benefits. No more. No less.
earned_vs_privilege_distinction.neither_punish_nor_privilege: A person should neither receive special lifetime benefits nor be financially punished for serving.
rejects: lifetime healthcare solely because someone held office
special retirement formulas unavailable to ordinary citizens
permanent taxpayer-funded privileges tied only to holding elected office
preserves: benefits earned under generally applicable contribution and eligibility rules
veterans’ services where the person independently qualifies under the same eligibility rules as other veterans
ordinary earned compensation already paid for work performed
service compensation and contributions that count like ordinary employment toward universal systems

end_political_aristocracy.summary: Reject the idea that public office creates a higher class of citizen.

equal_systems.rule: Government officials should live under the systems they create.
equal_systems.incentive: If legislators use the same systems as the people, they have a direct stake in making those systems work well.
systems: veterans’ services (where applicable under the same eligibility rules)

office_not_career_plan.rule: Public office exists to contribute to the republic, not to establish permanent employment within government.
office_not_career_plan.reinforces: Citizen-led government rather than a permanent governing class.

citizen_legislature.summary: The ideal legislature is composed of people who maintain roots in their communities rather than career politicians whose entire adult lives are spent inside government institutions.

compensation.problem_with_underpay: Often creates government dominated by the wealthy, retirees, owners who can afford absences, people supported by outside political organizations, or those using office as a pathway to future private income.
compensation.goal: Attract talented people from every economic background; remove incentives for corruption without creating a privileged governing class. A state legislator should not become wealthy through office, but a teacher or electrician should not face bankruptcy for serving.
standards: adjusted for travel and geographic burdens
prohibited from being changed by officeholders for their current terms
sufficient that ordinary citizens can afford to serve

cooling_off.summary: Limit the revolving door for a defined period after leaving office — paired with realistic pathways back into productive work.
may_restrict: representing private interests before agencies they recently oversaw
immediately joining companies they directly regulated
accepting jobs negotiated while exercising regulatory authority
cooling_off.tailoring_rule: Carefully tailored to reduce conflicts of interest without unnecessarily preventing people from earning a living. We cannot tell people to leave office, deny them ordinary employment, and then provide no transition.
cooling_off.legal_note: Duration, coverage, and exceptions require legal drafting and constitutional review — not specified as locked statutes here.

transparency.rule: Government service should be among the most transparent professions in society.

civic_honor.summary: Rather than rewarding politicians with extraordinary benefits, reward exemplary service through civic recognition. Honor becomes the reward — not lifelong privilege.

citizen_service_reforms.title: Guarantee civic-service leave
citizen_service_reforms.summary: Legally protected Public Service Leave after election or appointment to a qualifying position, analogous to military-service protections: protected leave, seniority continuation, anti-retaliation, return rights to same or comparable position, preservation of previously earned retirement rights, and continuation or portability of essential benefits. Employer need not hold every exact seat vacant indefinitely, but the person must not lose their profession for serving.

citizen_service_reforms.title: Public Service Replacement Fund
citizen_service_reforms.summary: Public fund to help pay temporary replacement staff, overtime, training, short-term professional services, substitute teachers or healthcare workers, and business continuity assistance — so democratic service costs are not shifted entirely onto employers. Strongest support for small businesses, farms, rural hospitals, schools, nonprofits, and employers below a defined size. Large corporations generally absorb ordinary civic leave without public subsidy.

citizen_service_reforms.title: Civic Enterprise Continuity Program
citizen_service_reforms.summary: For self-employed citizens and business owners: temporary management assistance, qualified interim operators, payroll support for replacement labor, low-interest continuity loans, tax credits for legitimate replacement expenses, business-planning assistance, and protection against losing public licenses because of service-related absence. Not a subsidy for failing businesses — tied to documented cost of temporary public service.

citizen_service_reforms.title: Pay officials enough to make service possible
citizen_service_reforms.summary: Compensation sufficient for ordinary working people to serve without financial harm — transparent, independent, responsibility-based, and locked against self-dealing for the current term.

citizen_service_reforms.title: Shorter, structured legislative sessions
citizen_service_reforms.summary: Predictable regular sessions, shorter policy blocks, designated committee weeks, remote preparation, limited secure remote participation for appropriate hearings, protected constituent-service periods, and emergency sessions restricted to genuine emergencies. Calendar published years in advance. Technology reduces unnecessary capital time without eliminating in-person deliberation.

citizen_service_reforms.title: Regional legislative work centers
citizen_service_reforms.summary: Regional civic centers for secure video participation, committee testimony, bill research, public-record access, constituent meetings, board participation, authorized remote legislative activity, and professional staff support — especially for rural representatives. Capital remains formal center; government becomes physically accessible throughout the state.

citizen_service_reforms.title: Professional nonpartisan support for every office
citizen_service_reforms.summary: Every legislator needs institutional (not party-owned) nonpartisan assistance in legal, fiscal, constitutional, drafting, data, community-impact, public communication, and ethics analysis — otherwise reducing career politicians transfers power to lobbyists, party staff, bureaucracies, and wealthy interests.

citizen_service_reforms.title: Civic leadership pipeline
citizen_service_reforms.summary: Open pathways from student civic service and youth councils through community organizations, municipal boards, civic-service credentials, commissions, county/regional leadership, and state responsibility — via civic academies, apprenticeships, fellowships, adult internships, and mentoring. No party controls entry.

citizen_service_reforms.title: Open boards and commissions to ordinary citizens
citizen_service_reforms.summary: Every vacancy publicly listed in one statewide portal with purpose, powers, workload, qualifications, compensation, term, appointing authority, conflicts rules, deadline, membership, and geography. Citizens create a Civic Service Profile. Appointments must not be limited to insiders known personally by elected officials.

citizen_service_reforms.title: Multiple levels of civic service
citizen_service_reforms.summary: Micro-service (hours/days), project service (weeks/months), term service (1–4 years), and professional public service careers — widening participation beyond those who make government their full-time identity.

citizen_service_reforms.title: Rotation without amnesia
citizen_service_reforms.summary: Prefer limits on consecutive terms and required intervals outside the same office over rigid lifetime bans that remove capable servants while strengthening lobbyists and bureaucracies. Preserve mentoring, knowledge transfer, and public archives. A legislator may serve limited consecutive terms, return to private life, and later serve again after a substantial break.

citizen_service_reforms.title: Remove financial penalties for serving
citizen_service_reforms.summary: Service must not cause loss of healthcare, retirement vesting, professional licensing, ordinary employment benefits, childcare, or family financial stability. Officials remain in universal systems; service compensation and contributions count like ordinary employment.

citizen_service_reforms.title: Family and caregiving support
citizen_service_reforms.summary: Reasonable childcare during sessions, eldercare support, justified family travel assistance, parental leave, limited remote participation, and predictable schedules — participation supports, not special political privileges. A government made only for people without caregiving responsibilities will not represent the public.

citizen_service_reforms.title: Protect against employer retaliation and political coercion
citizen_service_reforms.summary: Employers may not fire someone for running for lawful office, threaten promotion loss for civic service, pressure votes, require political loyalty, or use civic leave as punishment. Officials may not misuse leave protections to neglect legitimate work obligations before taking office. An independent public-service employment tribunal hears disputes quickly.

citizen_service_reforms.title: Return-to-community plans
citizen_service_reforms.summary: In the final year of service: career-transition support, recredentialing, return-to-work coordination, technical training, and business continuity planning — reducing temptation to turn office into permanent employment or immediately monetize public relationships through lobbying.

citizen_service_reforms.title: Restrict revolving-door employment with transition pathways
citizen_service_reforms.summary: Post-office restrictions paired with realistic pathways back into productive work.

citizen_service_reforms.title: Citizen Service Agreements
citizen_service_reforms.summary: Before taking office, a public agreement states duties, compensation, conflicts rules, attendance, transparency, benefit structure, return-to-employment protections, post-service restrictions, and accountability standards — so the public knows exactly what service requires and provides.

citizen_service_reforms.title: Build the government calendar around public participation
citizen_service_reforms.summary: Evening hearings, rotating regional hearings, hybrid testimony, published schedules, childcare at major proceedings, translation and disability access, and guaranteed public-comment pathways — for officeholders and the public they represent.

citizen_public_service_commission.summary: Independent of parties and elected leadership. Administers civic-service leave, employer reimbursement, business continuity, board recruitment, civic credentials, service agreements, compensation studies, return-to-career assistance, participation data, and anti-retaliation enforcement. Does not choose who wins elections — makes service practically accessible.

accountability_balance.rule: Make public service easier to enter—but not easier to abuse.
accountability_balance.status: A citizen legislator is not an amateur exempt from competence. They are a temporary constitutional trustee supported by professional systems.

citizen_public_service_test.purpose: Screen any proposed office benefit, access support, leave rule, compensation design, or post-office restriction.
questions: Does this create a privilege available only because someone held office, or a benefit earned under the same rules as similarly situated citizens?
Would officials live under the same healthcare, retirement, tax, and service systems they create?
Can an ordinary working person serve without sacrificing livelihood, business, family security, or retirement?
Are leave, replacement, and enterprise-continuity supports tied to documented service costs rather than open-ended subsidy?
Does institutional nonpartisan staff prevent power from shifting to lobbyists and parties?
Are post-office restrictions paired with dignified return-to-work pathways?
Does the design separate temporary democratic leadership from professional public administration?
Are citizen officials held to competence, ethics, attendance, and disclosure standards?
